items.label: Online Job Placement (PEL)
items.description: The Online Job Placement (PEL) website lets you browse job postings, apply for jobs, and create job alerts to receive offers.

items.label: Multi-service room at the Verdun Local Employment Centre
items.description: A place where you can carry out your own job search steps. Available to you: computer, photocopier, fax machine, phone, and documentation. Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday: 8:30 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4:30 p.m. Wednesday: 10 a.m. to noon and 1 p.m. to 4:30 p.m.

items.label: Grande Bibliothèque
items.description: On the 2nd floor, you can get information on Quebec government programs and services, employment support, and attend job search workshops.

items.label: Employment assistance services
items.description: Activities offered to equip you with job search techniques or to clarify your employment goal.

items.label: Workforce training measure
items.description: To take general, vocational, or technical training.

items.label: Job readiness project
items.description: To acquire skills in order to hold a job in a sustainable way.

items.label: Wage subsidy
items.description: To obtain financial assistance and encourage an employer to offer you a job.

items.label: Program to Support the Integration of Immigrants and Visible Minorities into Employment (PRIIME)
items.description: To gain a first work experience in Quebec in your field.

items.label: Support for Self-Employment
items.description: For people who want to start their own business or become self-employed.

items.label: Recognition of Prior Learning and Skills (RAC)
items.description: To have your prior learning officially recognized in order to obtain a diploma or certificate.

items.label: Directory of useful websites for job searching
